en.name: The Baptism of the Lord
en.summary: Commemorates Christ's baptism by John in the Jordan, marking the start of his public ministry and closing the Christmas season.
en.body: Observed on the Sunday following Epiphany, this feast commemorates Christ's baptism by John in the Jordan River, an event recorded in all four Gospels in which the heavens opened, the Holy Spirit descended upon Jesus in the form of a dove, and a voice from heaven declared him God's beloved Son, the first explicit Trinitarian revelation in the Gospel narrative. Although Jesus, being without sin, had no need of John's baptism of repentance, the Church has long understood his submission to it as an act of humility and solidarity with sinful humanity, and as the moment that formally inaugurated his public ministry. The feast marks the conclusion of the Christmas season in the liturgical calendar, after which Ordinary Time resumes.
